question: What are the exact Band-9 public insmod, rmmod, and modhandle entry points and lifecycle semantics?
prototype_hypothesis: insmod(path,module_name) returns a module handle after relocation and constructors; modhandle(name) resolves the registry handle; rmmod(handle) invokes destructors and releases module allocations
control_flow_evidence: The exact release vela_ap IDB contains the shared NSH failure-format string but no insmod, rmmod, or modhandle command strings or handlers.
Unlike the exact Band-10 firmware, Band-9 vela_ap contains no NuttX modlib source-path strings, ELF relocation/section/symbol diagnostics, or verified modlib_insert-style control flow.

A raw scan of every extracted Band-9 OTA image and filesystem file found no insmod or modhandle string and no modlib_insert/modlib_remove marker; the sole rmmod byte sequence was an unreferenced coincidence inside a watchface resource.bin.
The prior addresses and call graph in this record were from the Band-10 target and are not valid Band-9 evidence.
ownership_analysis: Unresolved. Current static evidence indicates that the release vela_ap may not link the NuttX ET_REL modlib loader at all; a different proven loading boundary is required before constructor/destructor ownership can be specified.
unsafe_assumptions: Band-10 modlib addresses, globals, registry layout, and wrapper signatures must not be copied into Band-9.
The Band-9 target.toml loader profile is not proof that the exact firmware implements that profile.
The Band-9 supervisor platform remains incomplete until an exact release-firmware loader boundary is proven.
recommended_probe: First prove that the exact Band-9 release firmware can load an ELF32 ET_REL module through a stock command or API. If it can, capture that command's call chain and recover its public load/lookup/remove ABI; otherwise define and verify a different target loader architecture rather than inventing modlib addresses.
